newsitem.title: UK: BA Regional wants big pay cuts - Labour.
newsitem.headline: BA Regional wants big pay cuts - Labour.

text.p: British Airways Regional is asking its cabin staff to accept pay cuts of up to 40 percent as part of a cost-cutting drive, the Labour Party said.
Citing an internal document, the main opposition party said BA Regional, wholly owned by British Airways Plc, also wanted to slash overtime payments.

"British Airways is a vastly profitable company and I find it deplorable that they are asking loyal staff, who have already made big sacrifices to make BA Regional work, to accept these huge pay cuts," Brian Wilson, head of Labour's rebuttal unit, said. He called on BA to reconsider the proposed cuts.
BA Regional operates most of BA's domestic services as well as transatlantic and European routes out of Birmingham, Manchester and Glasgow, where its cabin staff are based.

Under the proposed pay cuts, according to Labour, a steward with seven years' service would be paid 7,920 stg a year instead of 11,710 stg. The most senior cabin service directors would have their pay cut to 18,694 stg from 22,870 stg.
Laura De Vere, a spokeswoman for BA Regional, confirmed that the company had suggested pay cuts as a way of reducing cabin crew costs to the "market price" but was open to alternatives.

"Some proposals have been tabled to cabin crew... but the consultation process has only just begun and we're seeking alternative ideas and initiatives from every employee in every department," she said.
"While you cannot rule out pay cuts as part of the efficiency drive, no specific figures have been determined or agreed with any department," she added.

De Vere said BA Regional, which lost close to 20 million stg last year and was likely to be in the red again this year, needed to cut costs in part to fund heavy investment in new aircraft to replace its fleet of Boeing 737s.
"If we are uncompetitive and seen off by the competition because they have lower costs, then clearly we cannot continue to pay staff up to 30 percent above the market rate," she said.
